thread:
Maya K: Quick design check — uploaded a couple of dark-mode passes for the console charts + token heatmap. wondering if we should treat heatmap as a separate token palette or reuse series colors. figma: https://figma.com/file/abcd (screenshots attached) :eyes:
Samir P: glanced — overall looks good. main thing: series colors are too close when saturation is low. hard to scan small multiples.
Lisa T: agree. on dark backgrounds we lose perceived contrast. do we have WCAG ratios for each palette? low-sat teal is <3:1 on the panel bg. :warning:
Maya K: hmm, we should avoid <4.5:1 for small UI text, but for chart series maybe 3:1 is acceptable? needs design system callout.
Ryan G: for charts I prefer using perceptually-distinct hues + different tonal weights rather than rely only on saturation. also consider pattern overlays (dashed, dotted) for accessibility/print.
Samir P: pattern idea is neat — especially for people who print or for color-blind folks. does that play nicely with the realtime micro-interactions (hover, focus)?
Lisa T: it can. hover can toggle fill opacity and remove pattern. but baseline must be readable without hover. also prefer using a divergent palette for heatmaps (cool -> warm) rather than sequential blues used for series. prevents accidental mapping confusion.
Maya K: proposal: keep series palette as 6 hues (muted but distinct) + 3 pattern fills for high-density overlays. heatmap = custom divergent token palette. also add a high-contrast theme toggle under Accessibility in console. copy: "Dark (default)" and "Dark (high contrast)"? thoughts?
Ryan G: copy tweak: maybe "Dark — balanced" and "Dark — high contrast" reads better inline. shorter labels in the theme picker.
Samir P: +1 for shorthand. also a tiny UX nit: when you switch themes the chart legend currently flashes because we re-render with full anim. can we fade color only? makes the transition less jarring.
Maya K: noted. i can add a motion spec: fade colors 160ms ease-out, no layout jump.
Lisa T: color tokens — can you share CSS vars? i'll run them through contrast checker and the color-blind simulator. also need token names that communicate intent (e.g., --chart-series-1 rather than --muted-teal).
Aria Bot: color tokens generated from Figma palette: computed contrast ratios attached.
Aria Bot: ```css
/* theme: dark-balanced */
:root {
  --bg: #0b0d0f; /* 14.9:1 */
  --panel: #0f1214; /* 12.3:1 */
  --text-primary: #e6eef2; /* 13.5:1 */
  --chart-series-1: #6cc6ff; /* 4.2:1 */
  --chart-series-2: #7be0c6; /* 3.1:1 */
  --chart-series-3: #ffd08a; /* 3.6:1 */
  --chart-series-4: #ff9fb6; /* 3.0:1 */
  --chart-series-5: #c6a6ff; /* 3.4:1 */
  --chart-series-6: #7aa6ff; /* 3.2:1 */
  --heatmap-cold: #1b2840; /* diverging start */
  --heatmap-warm: #ff6b3d; /* diverging end */
}
```
Samir P: thanks — looking at these, series-2 and series-4 are borderline. can we nudge series-2 a touch warmer and desaturate series-4?
Lisa T: if we nudge, retest against panel bg. also confirm legend swatch size — at 8px it becomes indistinguishable for similar hues. recommend 12px min for clarity.
Maya K: noted. i'll update tokens and increase legend swatch to 12px. also adding pattern tokens: `--pattern-dots`, `--pattern-hatch`, `--pattern-diagonal` that overlay at 14% opacity.
Ryan G: UX edge-case — stacked area charts: patterns look noisy. maybe only apply patterns for line/bar/heatmap, not areas.
Samir P: agree. we can fallback to high-contrast brightness tweak for areas.
Lisa T: accessibility checklist: 1) contrast ratios for all tokens 2) legend swatch size 3) pattern toggles + user setting 4) keyboard focus states for theme picker 5) announce theme change for screen readers.
Maya K: perfect list. i'll push a new figma page with updated tokens + a lightweight prototype (no anim) by EOD. can reviewers try the prototype with these three quick checks: colorblind sim, keyboard-only nav, and a11y contrast audit? :paintbrush:
Samir P: can do. i'll focus on chart readablity and legend size.
Lisa T: i'll run contrast/a11y checks and post results.
Ryan G: i'll test interactions and transitions (fade-only).
Maya K: thanks all — super helpful. will follow up with the new file and a small changelog entry for release notes (copy: "Improved dark-mode chart legibility + accessible heatmap palette"). :tada:
